title: Commute transit wait time uniform interval
scenario_markdown: A passenger arrives at a transit stop where the wait time $X$ until the next express shuttle is uniformly distributed between 0 and 20 minutes ($X \sim U(0, 20)$). Find the probability that the passenger waits between 5 and 12 minutes.

stages.prompt_markdown: What is the constant probability density height $f(x)$ for wait times within the support interval $[0, 20]$ minutes?

options.hint_markdown: Total area under the PDF must equal 1, so the height is the reciprocal of the width: $1/(b-a)$.
Divide 1 by the width of the interval $(20 - 0)$.

stages.explanation_markdown: For $U(a, b)$, the density is constant: $f(x) = \frac{1}{b - a} = \frac{1}{20} = 0.05$ per minute for $0 \le x \le 20$.

stages.prompt_markdown: Calculate $P(5 \le X \le 12) = \frac{12 - 5}{20 - 0}$. Enter as a decimal or percentage.
How does the probability $P(5 \le X \le 12)$ compare to the strict inequality $P(5 < X < 12)$?

options.text_markdown: They are exactly identical ($0.35$) because individual endpoints carry zero probability in any continuous distribution.
$P(5 \le X \le 12)$ is strictly larger because it includes the points 5 and 12
options.hint_markdown: In continuous distributions, $P(X = 5) = 0$ and $P(X = 12) = 0$, so including endpoints changes nothing.

options.text_markdown: They cannot be compared without knowing whether the shuttle schedule is exact
options.hint_markdown: Mathematically, for any continuous random variable, $P(X \in [c, d]) = P(X \in (c, d))$.

stages.explanation_markdown: In continuous probability, single points have zero measure: $P(X = 5) = 0$ and $P(X = 12) = 0$. Therefore, $P(5 \le X \le 12) = P(5 < X < 12) = 0.35$.
